newsitem.title: USA: Draft limit raised again at Port of New Orleans.
newsitem.headline: Draft limit raised again at Port of New Orleans.

text.p: The draft limit on vessels navigating the Mississippi River near New Orleans was raised to 42 feet Wednesday, and could be increased to a normal level of 46 feet if no problems occur, Coast Guard officials said.
"The Coast Guard had increased the draft to 42 feet," said Commander Ken Parris of the Coast Guard's Marine Safety Office in New Orleans.
Draft restrictions have been in place since Saturday, when a grain freighter, the Bright Field, lost control and plowed into a waterfront shopping complex near the city's French Quarter.

After closing the port immediately following the accident, the Coast Guard has gradually allowed larger ships to navigate up and down-river in the vicinity of the wreck. Late Tuesday, a 40-foot draft vessel successfully navigated through the port.
Parris said the Coast Guard had yet to do a test run under the new 42-foot draft limit. If no problems result under the latest restrictions, he said, the maximum would likely be raised to 46 feet.
"As soon as a 42-footer goes by, if there are no indications of any problems, it will be raised," he said.

While maritime traffic was permitted in both directions, it was required to alternate between inbound and outbound vessels, and some delays were noted. At midday Wednesday, two vessels were reportedly waiting to enter the port area bound up-river.

Meanwhile, divers continued to search beneath the wreck as the Coast Guard sought to determine how to remove the Bright Field from the river. The freighter was being held in place by tugboats because it was thought to be supporting part of the damaged wharf.
While efforts to shore up the wharf have begun, it was not yet known when the freighter would be removed, officials said.

The 735-foot Bright Field, owned by Cosco Hong Kong, was carrying 64,000 tons of corn when it rammed into the riverbank on Saturday. At least 116 people were injured as a result of the collison, but no deaths have been reported.
-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
